scope_note: Design only. Nothing here authorizes a real binding write, a login session, a page run or a platform call. Order payment and carrier-acceptance reads are NOT prerequisites for general policy binding and are not designed here.

q1_session_self_identity_evidence_availa.question: What platform identity evidence can the current code obtain from the session itself?
q1_session_self_identity_evidence_availa.answer: None. No implemented code path reads a platform-self identity (shop/mall id, seller account id) from the page, the protocol payload or the authenticated session. Every identifier the runtime uses today is generated by the application itself and therefore proves 'which local runtime object', not 'which PDD shop/account'.

evidence.note: stores a local display name and a platform enum; carries no platform external reference
the schema itself documents this field as 'Fast Sheep local Shop.id only; never a platform seller or account identity'; resolution fails closed for missing/blank/disabled/non-PDD

evidence.fields: shops.id = shop-<epoch_ms>-<4 digits>, type=pdd, name='Controlled PDD Runtime (local only)'
evidence.note: mints a purely local id; refuses to create a second PDD shop; writes no merchant/store/platform_account row

evidence.fields: sessionId, shopId, documentGeneration, observerId, observerLifecycleId, cdpSessionId, requestId, url, webContents
evidence.note: binds a message to a view/document generation; shopId here is the local shop id, not a platform id
the transport contract states ownership must never come from payload fields, the selected customer or the page URL; these are decoded as message content only
the authenticated PDD session lives in this partition, but nothing in the repository reads a logged-in platform identity from it
evidence.persisted: Electron partition storage (not read for identity)

q1_session_self_identity_evidence_availa.gap: GAP (registered, not invented): there is no session-self platform identity probe. A future verification step must obtain platform identity evidence through one explicitly authorized read-only observation, and its provenance must be recorded - see q6 for the schema gap that blocks recording it.
do_not_do: do not treat the local shop id, the partition name or the document/session ids as platform identity
do not promote mallName/uid/shop_id from payloads into identity evidence
do not guess an undocumented platform endpoint or field name

q2_owner_declaration_to_session_evidence.question: How should the Owner-declared identifier (木易先生) be linked to session evidence auditably?
q2_owner_declaration_to_session_evidence.rule: The declaration is stored verbatim as OWNER_DECLARED material. A binding may only be recorded when an independently obtained session/platform evidence value matches a declared reference under an approved comparison rule; the display name alone, by itself or by equality with another name, can never make a binding pass.

comparison_rule_design.name_equality: INSUFFICIENT - never sufficient on its own
allowed_evidence_classes: platform account/shop reference observed from the authenticated session itself (future, not implemented)
an Owner-supplied platform external reference that the Owner states is the platform's own identifier for that shop, when the platform exposes no separate numeric id
comparison_rule_design.reference_format: opaque text; no numeric-format requirement and no format guessing (platform_accounts.external_ref is TEXT and nullable)
comparison_rule_design.recorded_distinction: declared value, evidence value, comparison rule, comparison outcome and evidence timestamp are recorded separately; a name-only match is recorded as UNVERIFIED_WEAK, not VERIFIED
comparison_rule_design.name_never_identity: a shop name (or any hash of it) is never stored as a platform-verified id and never used as a lookup key for binding

internal_identity.merchant: merchants(id, name) - trusted scope comes from bootstrap, never from a payload
internal_identity.store: stores(id, merchant_id, name, platform) - internal store id is application-minted
internal_identity.platform_account: platform_accounts(id, merchant_id, platform, external_ref) - internal account id plus an optional opaque external reference
internal_identity.relation_gap: platform_accounts has NO store_id column and stores has NO external reference column, so today a platform account cannot be related to a store at all (see q6)

separation_of_concerns.internal_ids: merchant_id / store_id / platform_account_id are internal; they are never derived from a platform value
separation_of_concerns.platform_external_reference: stored separately (platform_accounts.external_ref), remains opaque, and is never used as a primary key
separation_of_concerns.session_binding: runtime only (sessionId + documentGeneration), never persisted as identity

existing_validation_precedent.what_it_proves: secrets are bound to an internal platform_accounts.id via a SHA-256-derived SecretStore key, with fail-closed checks for invalid id, missing account, id mismatch, merchant-scope mismatch and platform mismatch
existing_validation_precedent.what_it_does_not_prove: it never reads a platform external identity, so it does not verify that the account is the Owner's shop
existing_validation_precedent.reuse: the same fail-closed shape (internal id + trusted merchant scope + platform check) is the right pattern for a binding record

q4_rejection_rules: cross-store: reject when the requested store id is not owned by the trusted merchant scope, or (once the relation exists) when the account is bound to a different store
cross-account: reject when the evidence value belongs to a different platform account than the one being bound
missing evidence: no evidence value -> binding state stays DECLARED / UNVERIFIED; never inferred from naming, timing or ordering
binding conflict: an already-bound account (or a store already bound to another account under the same platform) -> reject, keep the existing binding, never silently replace or merge

session switch / reload: a binding derived from runtime evidence expires with its session and document generation; after a session switch or document reload the previous evidence is invalid and the binding must be re-established (evidence is not inherited)
name-only match: reject as VERIFIED; may be recorded at most as UNVERIFIED_WEAK
invalid or blank identifiers: reject with an explicit reason code, never normalise, trim or hash an identifier into a key
uncertain provenance: when the evidence source is not the explicitly authorized read-only observation, the outcome is UNKNOWN, not a best guess

read_only_verification_actions.status: NOT_AUTHORIZED - listed only to define the future minimum
actions: one explicitly authorized, read-only observation inside the already-controlled single-store session that yields the platform's own identity value for the logged-in shop/account
a human-visible confirmation step for the Owner (bind this declared shop to this observed reference) - the Owner, not the code, supplies the declaration that ties a name to the reference

write_actions.status: NOT_AUTHORIZED - requires a separate implementation authorization plus a governed schema decision
minimum_entities: stores (the internal store for the controlled shop)
platform_accounts (internal account row for the PDD shop, with the opaque external_ref)
a binding-verification record (new, or an approved extension of platform_accounts) carrying: verification state, evidence kind, evidence reference and observed_at
a policy-version registration row (durable equivalent of the sealed in-memory registry)

q6_schema_sufficiency.verdict: PARTIALLY SUFFICIENT - reuse first, one precise gap must be decided before any binding write
reusable_today: stores / merchants / platform_accounts tables (migration 0005) cover the internal identity triple, and platform_accounts.external_ref is opaque TEXT (no numeric-format requirement)
PlatformAccountRepository and StoreRepository ports already exist and are exercised by tests

the canonical fastwork:domain:identity-lock schema already models merchantId/storeId/platformAccountId as RESOLVED | UNKNOWN | UNRESOLVED and carries runtimeEvidence{sessionId, documentGeneration, selectedCustomerObservation}, so 'not yet resolved' has a canonical representation that needs no new field
precise_gaps: no store<->platform_account relation: platform_accounts has no store_id and stores has no external reference column, so a cross-store check cannot be expressed today
no verification provenance on platform_accounts: there is no column for verification state (DECLARED / UNVERIFIED_WEAK / VERIFIED / REVOKED), evidence kind, evidence reference or observed_at
no persisted binding-evidence entity for session/document-scoped evidence
no durable policy-version table (the sealed Lane B registry is in-memory only; a SQLite table would need a governed canonical schema change and a frozen manifest update)
q6_schema_sufficiency.constraint_followed: no schema was changed or proposed as an ad-hoc field; no fake verification column was invented in code or in this design

expected_files_if_authorized: packages/contracts/schemas/domain/platform-identity-binding.schema.json (only if a new contract is approved; otherwise extend the existing identity contract set)
resources/persistence/migrations/0008_*.sql (append-only; only if the governed schema decision approves it)
apps/desktop/src/main/services/shop-binding-service.ts (fail-closed binding service reusing the credential-reference pattern)
acceptance_cases: declaration-only: registering the Owner declaration yields DECLARED / UNVERIFIED and never a binding
name-only match is refused as VERIFIED and recorded at most as UNVERIFIED_WEAK
evidence from a different platform account is refused (cross-account)
evidence for a store outside the trusted merchant scope is refused (cross-store)
missing evidence keeps the state UNVERIFIED and writes nothing
a second binding for an already-bound account/store is refused and the existing binding is preserved
after a session switch or document reload the previous evidence no longer validates the binding
an opaque (non-numeric) external reference is accepted and stored verbatim, and never used as a primary key
no AI, send, order or logistics port is introduced by the binding service
all acceptance cases run against synthetic fixtures and an in-memory/fixture store; no real page, no platform call
stop_conditions: required evidence source is not authorized -> stop, record BLOCKED, do not approximate identity
a binding would need a new schema and the governed schema decision is not approved -> stop, do not add an ad-hoc column
any step would need a real page, a platform call, a login, AI, send or a production write -> stop, that is outside this unit
a step would generalize into full store management, SKU management or order logistics -> stop, out of scope
evidence conflicts with an existing binding -> keep the existing binding, record the conflict, do not silently replace
explicitly_out_of_scope: full store/shop management or onboarding UI
order-level expected/committed shipping date derivation (still PRODUCT_DECISION_REQUIRED)
durable policy persistence design (separate governed decision)

state_separation.binding_verification: may become VERIFIED once an authorized evidence-based check passes; says nothing about the policy
state_separation.policy_content_approval: already OWNER_CONFIRMED for the declared policy text (content only)
state_separation.policy_effectiveness: still DRAFT / NOT_EFFECTIVE; no effective window exists
state_separation.runtime_activation: NOT_AUTHORIZED and not implied by any of the above
state_separation.rule: a successful binding never triggers content approval, effectiveness or runtime activation; each is a separate state transition with its own authorization

already_confirmed_not_reopened.applicability: regular stock only (declared scope; not extended to all goods)
already_confirmed_not_reopened.weekend_holiday_handling: counted in the continuous duration, no automatic extension
already_confirmed_not_reopened.note: these are Owner-confirmed content facts and are not re-opened by this design

timezone_and_calendar_note: A continuous-hours rule needs no business calendar and no timezone. A timezone (candidate Asia/Shanghai) and any business calendar become requirements only if a future approved rule interprets local dates or cut-off times; no cut-off rule is approved and none is assumed here.
owner_inputs_still_missing: an approved platform external reference for the controlled shop, or the platform's own identity value obtained by the authorized read-only observation
Owner confirmation of the exact binding statement (declare shop / bind to observed reference)
the governed decision on how binding provenance is stored (see q6 gaps)
next_step: Controller/Owner decision on (a) the authorized read-only identity observation and (b) the binding-provenance storage decision; implementation stays blocked until both are settled
